q: Agent context files are common, and many of them stand still through hundreds of commits.
r: Include: measures currency and staleness of AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md context files in 452 repositories and proposes a governance discipline for coding agents.

q: We analyzed 2,870 instruction-file pull requests across 2,246 repositories.
r: IC1: studies how humans and AI reviewers review changes to instruction files, not the effect of context files on coding-agent cost or quality; relevance to RQ2-RQ4 doubtful.

q: We also deployed MemoSync with nine developers on their own projects for one week.
r: Include: controlled user study of agent memory management for coding agents on full-stack projects against a Markdown memory-file baseline.

q: We selected 40,585 actively maintained repositories through metadata filtering, classified them using GPT-5.2 to identify 36,710 as belonging to engineered software projects, and systematically detected configuration artifacts in these repositories.
r: Include: dataset of context files, skills, rules and hooks configuring agentic coding tools (group b).

q: We collect a dataset of 12,110 .cursorrules files from 11,427 open-source GitHub repositories.
r: Include: empirical study of Cursor rule files (context mechanism for coding agents), 2026.

q: we analyze 15,549 agentic PRs from 148 projects in the AIDev dataset. Using the three dimensions, we compare each project before and after the creation of the instruction files.
r: Include: measures the effect of instruction files on agentic PR merge rate, churn and time to merge.

q: we characterize this phenomenon across 247,694 instruction lifetimes in 1,867 repositories: agentic prompts grow nearly monotonically, more than tripling over their lifetime
r: Include: studies growth of CLAUDE.md files and evaluates instruction following and prompt size with coding agents.

q: We measure the effects of Skill evolution on effectiveness on 21 models (16 open-weight and five closed) and on cost on 20 of them
r: Include: measures effect of Skill revisions on effectiveness and token cost of coding agents (group b).
